key_insight: Transient ion current (TIC) in perovskite solar cells is often limited by transport-layer capacitance, not just the perovskite ion density, so measured ionic parameters can be strongly biased by the contacts.
engineering_relevance: Accurate ion quantification in PSCs requires accounting for transport-layer thickness, doping, and interfacial charge storage to avoid overestimating ionic density and mobility.
method: Varied C60 electron-transport-layer thickness in p-i-n cells
Varied Spiro-OMeTAD hole-transport-layer doping in n-i-p cells
Used simulations and thickness-trend extrapolation to infer the absorber's ionic properties
evidence_signal: Systematic experiments across both device architectures confirmed that TIC depends strongly on transport-layer properties and that extrapolating to the transport-layer-free limit can recover the absorber’s ionic conductivity.
watch_item: TIC-based ion extraction can be inflated by transport-layer capacitance, ion penetration into TLs, or slow release of trapped carriers, so raw TIC values should not be interpreted as direct ion densities.
paper_title: Overcoming Transport Layer Bottlenecks to Quantify Ionic Parameters from Transient Ion Current Measurements of Perovskite Solar Cells
